name: inflight
description: One snapshot S1 initiated at n1 while transfers are genuinely in flight. The marker interleaving places t1 on the n1->n2 channel AHEAD of n2 recording (so t1 is already credited and the channel capture is empty), t2 on n2->n3 BEFORE n3 records (captured 5), and t3 on n1->n3 AFTER n3 already closed that channel on the marker (post-cut, not captured). No process is ever paused: n2 issues t2 after the round opens. Hand-derived numbers: locals 30+45+20=95, captured in-flight 5, global cut 95+5=100. See docs/SCENARIOS.md.

steps.note: t1: n1 debits a 30->20; envelope enters durable outbox n1->n2
t1 IN FLIGHT n1->n2
n1 records local (a20,b10)=30, markers queued in outbox
marker S1 IN FLIGHT n1->n2, strictly behind t1 (same outbox, FIFO)
marker S1 IN FLIGHT n1->n3
t2: the system stays live while S1 is open (no global pause)
t2 IN FLIGHT n2->n3 before n3 records
FIFO head t1 delivered: n2 credits d 30->40
marker now: n2 FIRST hears of S1, records local (d40,e10)=50, closes n1->n2 EMPTY, queues its markers
t3: n1 keeps transacting after recording; marker to n3 already in flight so t3 is enqueued AFTER it
t3 IN FLIGHT n1->n3 behind the S1 marker
marker S1 n2->n1 in flight
marker S1 n2->n3 in flight behind t2
marker first on n1->n3: n3 records local (g10,h10)=20, closes n1->n3 EMPTY
t3 then: channel n1->n3 ALREADY CLOSED by the marker, so t3 is post-cut (not captured) and simply credits h 10->14
t2: captured in n2->n3 (5) and credited g 10->15
marker closes n2->n3 with [t2]=5
n1 closes inbound n2->n1
marker n3->n1 in flight
marker n3->n2 in flight
n1 closes inbound n3->n1: n1 complete
n2 closes inbound n3->n2: n2 complete
